Getting started

Pick the way you want to use Pare. Each one takes about five minutes.

I have... Use Start here
an ASP.NET Core app the MSBuild package Your first web app
a static site, or any non-.NET project the pare command Your first static site
C# code that wants to strip types the library Using the library
Rust, Go, Python or similar the C library Using libpare from C and other languages

Requirements

To use You need
the pare command from a release archive nothing
the pare command as a .NET tool the .NET 10 SDK (on platforms without a prebuilt binary, the tool runs on the .NET 10 runtime)
Extrode.Pare.Build or Extrode.Pare.AspNetCore the .NET 10 SDK, a project that targets net10.0
Visual Studio Visual Studio 2026 (MSBuild 18). Visual Studio 2022 cannot build net10.0 projects.
libpare a C compiler or an FFI in your language

Pare builds on Windows, macOS and Linux. dotnet build works from the command line, Rider and VS Code. The prebuilt binaries cover osx-arm64, osx-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, linux-musl-x64, linux-musl-arm64, win-x64 and win-arm64.

Install

NuGet packages (for .NET projects):

bash 
dotnet add package Extrode.Pare.Build
dotnet add package Extrode.Pare.AspNetCore

Open the project file afterwards and add PrivateAssets="all" to the Extrode.Pare.Build reference, so projects that reference yours do not inherit the build step.

The command line tool:

Download pare-<version>-<rid>.tar.gz (.zip on Windows) from the releases page, unpack it and put the folder on your PATH. It needs no .NET. Or install the .NET tool: dotnet tool install -g Extrode.Pare.Cli. It needs the .NET 10 runtime and starts slower than the archive.

Check that it works

bash 
echo 'const n: number = 1;' | pare --stdin

You should see the line back with the type replaced by spaces:

text 
const n         = 1;
